HCP2 Forest Review
Project Ember · Epic 5 · Human checkpoint 2 · round 2

The forest is real

● Awaiting your comprehensive review

Three Queens with every tree Terrain places, now with west-Cascades species mixes, a stand structure under the canopy, trees modelled from their growth forms, and near / mid / far detail tiers that bring the full forest back inside the frame budget.

Kittitas County, WA · 10 m · 5,856,630 trees · UE 5.8.3, SM6 + Nanite · 2026-09-28

Your round-1 notes, and what changed

You saidWhat changed
"Too dense"Each tree now draws a crown class (dominant to suppressed) and a height under the canopy top, and its crown scales with its size. Mean height fell from 34 m to 23 m, and there is a real understory. Rendered canopy cover now tracks LANDFIRE: 50 % where it says 50 %, 82 % where it says 82 %.
"Pine should be rare"One species mix per LANDFIRE forest type. Three Queens is western hemlock 26 %, Pacific silver fir 24 %, Douglas-fir 17 %, mountain hemlock 12 %, redcedar 8 %, and ponderosa 1.2 %. Alder and cottonwood grow along streams, vine maple in shrubland.
"Couldn't see any wind"A locked-off clip with the camera still, the sun behind it and the crowns against the sky. Twig flutter now rides on top of the sway.
"Up close trees look cartoonish"15 species modelled from how they grow: trunk flare, branch whorls, droop, nodding hemlock tops, flat needle sprays, pine tufts, broadleaf crowns. Four variants each. Bark is a flat colour until you have licensed scans.
"Radius isn't going to be our only solve"Near / mid / far tiers per 320 m cell, two Nanite foliage settings, and a written plan (D11) with a budget line for every system, including fire, smoke and weather.

Still exact: the renderer reproduces all 24,814 teanaway and 5,856,630 Three Queens trees from Terrain.

Stats and budget

Pose, 1440pRound 1New trees, no tiersNow
Aerial oblique, 2.2 km outGPU 7.9 ms · 3.3 GBGPU 12.0 ms · 3.5 GBGPU 5.7 ms · p95 8.7 ms · 3.4 GB
Low flyover, 120 m up—GPU 22.8 msGPU 7.8 ms · p95 10.3 ms · 3.3 GB

Budget: 16.7 ms (60 fps) and 4 GB. Near trees (under 500 m) draw in full with wind and live shadows. From 500 m to 4 km a lite copy of the same tree draws with no wind and no understory. Past 4 km the terrain colouring carries the forest.

Known issues

  1. lookScenes read dark. Exposure has been fixed at −2 EV since HCP0, when it was tuned on bare terrain. Dense conifer canopy is dark by nature, so the forests look like late evening.
  2. feelStutter. About 12 frames in 300 spike to 35–125 ms while the render thread waits on the GPU. p95 is inside budget, but you would feel it flying the camera. Profiling is scheduled before HCP6.
  3. tiersDetail steps at 320 m cell edges while moving. A cross-fade is planned, not built.
  4. rangeTrees end at 4 km. Distant ridgelines have no treed silhouette yet (D11 far tier and surround rings).
  5. assetBark is a flat placeholder colour until licensed scans arrive.

Decisions for you

  1. Tree source going forward: more generated variants, modular crown sections, or SpeedTree / library trees under an ADR. The pipeline works with any of them.
  2. Exposure and lighting pass: brighten the forests now (every golden gets re-blessed), or wait until the fire visuals exist?
  3. Density: does the low flyover now read like this country?
  4. Wind: is the amount right now that you can see it?
  5. D11 plan: agree with the tiers, the per-system budget table and the world-context rings?
